title: 400 People Danced to Death — The Cure Made It Worse
description:
In July 1518, Frau Troffea began dancing alone in a Strasbourg street. No music. No reason. She didn't stop. Within a week, 34 others joined her, feet bleeding, bodies moving without rest.

City physicians ruled out demonic possession and prescribed more dancing. The council built a stage, hired musicians, and cleared guildhalls as dance floors. By August, over 400 people danced until they collapsed from strokes, heart attacks, and exhaustion — some accounts reporting 15 deaths a day.

The outbreak finally ended in September after survivors were taken to a mountain shrine. Modern theories suggest ergot fungus, mass stress, or mass psychogenic illness, but Strasbourg's own records describe a trance no one could break. Five centuries later, no one knows what truly pulled them into the street.
